messages:
Ryan M: Quick heads-up — found a noisy alert pattern when tenants <500q/day hit our SLO window. Lots of churn from transient spikes.
Divya P: Ugh, seen that. Which alert specifically? per-route p99 latency or error-budget burn?
Ryan M: Error-budget burn alerts. They fire on 5m window then quiet backoff doesn't help because each small tenant resets counters.
Olivia S: Can we do a decay or smoothing per-tenant? ie if signal > threshold but volume low, apply a longer decay so we don't spam.
Ben K: Agree. Proposal: add a tenant-aware decay factor and a min-sample requirement. e.g. require >= N requests in window OR sustained across M windows.
Sam L: Want to avoid making users think their SLOs are useless. Maybe show in console that alert suppressed due to low volume. Transparency in UI.
Divya P: For API, how would that look? current notify policy proto is flat. We'd need fields like `min_hits` and `decay_minutes` per-route/tenant.
Ryan M: Sketch:
```
{
  "route_id": "generate-v1",
  "notify_policy": {
    "threshold_pct": 0.99,
    "min_hits": 50,
    "decay_minutes": 30
  }
}
```
Ben K: That seems reasonable. Also add `suppress_reason` in the notify webhook payload so downstream tools know why it was suppressed.
Olivia S: UX: Console preview should show a mock timeline when you toggle min_hits. Right now preview assumes infinite traffic.
Sam L: Telemetry ask — emit `slo.suppressed` events with tags: tenant_id, route_id, reason=min_hits|decay|quiet_window. This helps tune defaults.
Divya P: Important edge-case: bursty bots that send 60 reqs in 1s then nothing. min_hits would pass but still not meaningful. Maybe require hits spread across at least 2 distinct sub-windows.
Ryan M: Good call. Add `min_windows`: number of sub-windows within the main window that must have >= X hits.
Ben K: Implementation note: our realtime aggregator can calculate windows cheaply but needs config routing. Could default to `min_hits=20, min_windows=2` for tenants under 1k q/day.
Olivia S: Can we add an override toggle per-tenant in console (force alerts even if low volume)? Enterprise customers may want it.
Sam L: Yes, expose an override with an audit log entry.
Divya P: Who owns the API change? Ben + Ryan to spec. I'll follow up on telemetry and console UX flows.
Ryan M: I'll open a draft PR for the API contract + aggregator behavior. cc @notify-bot to add a sampling metric.
notify-bot: deploy-notify: Created metric `slo.suppressed.count` (env=staging). Link: https://metrics/redwood/slo.suppressed
Ben K: Thanks. Next steps: Ben/Ryan to post a short design doc, Olivia to wire console preview mock, Divya to propose telemetry schema. Decide defaults in the doc.
Olivia S: I'll prototype the preview tomorrow and drop screenshots in this thread.
Sam L: Also update runbooks to explain suppression vs real alerts.
Ryan M: Awesome. Thanks all :) :thumbsup:
